First step at which two evolution intervals overlap

Source: R/compare2.R
overlap_step.Rd

Scans the two curves of a compare2 comparison forward from \(n = 1\) and returns the first step at which their intervals overlap: before it, the state at the previous time changes the prediction. This is the criterion of the methods paper (Section 6.3), applied to evolution intervals (P2est fit) or to percentile bootstrap intervals (P2boot fit).

Usage

overlap_step(x)

Arguments

x

A two-group "msm2pred" with interval bounds.

Value

A list: first overlapping step n and time s = n + 1; the leading separated-step count separated_steps; per-step overlap and signed separation (= max lower - min upper, > 0 when separated); and the two groups.

Examples

st   <- c("A", "B", "C")                                 # C is absorbing
tens <- array(0, c(3, 3, 3), dimnames = list(st, st, st))
tens["B", "B", "A"] <- 0.6; tens["B", "C", "A"] <- 0.4
tens["B", "B", "B"] <- 0.3; tens["B", "C", "B"] <- 0.7
tens["C", "C", ]    <- 1
first <- matrix(0, 3, 3, dimnames = list(st, st)); first["A", "B"] <- 1

set.seed(1)
panel <- simulate2(500, tens, first, init = c(A = 1, B = 0, C = 0))
fit <- P2est(prep2(panel))
cmp <- compare2(fit, h = c("A", "B"), j = "B", l = "B", nsteps = 6)
overlap_step(cmp)
#> $n
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $s
#> [1] 4
#> 
#> $separated_steps
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $overlap
#>     1     2     3     4     5     6 
#> FALSE FALSE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE  TRUE 
#> 
#> $separation
#>            1            2            3            4            5            6 
#>  0.224601660  0.030557457 -0.002568936 -0.004577489 -0.002628205 -0.001208199 
#> 
#> $groups
#> [1] "A" "B"
#>
